cold_email.subject: Interest in Full Time Educator / Clarendon (Contract until January 2027) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Full Time Educator / Clarendon (Contract until January 2027) opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Administrative Support Coordinator I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear San Diego State University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Support Coordinator I opportunity with San Diego State University at San Diego State University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. cold_email.subject: Interest in Pre-ETS Instructor - Alcorn County, MS — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Public Consulting Group Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Pre-ETS Instructor - Alcorn County, MS opportunity with Public Consulting Group at Public Consulting Group.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Assistant Sponsored Research Officer - Proposal and Award Acceptance — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Northwestern University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Assistant Sponsored Research Officer - Proposal and Award Acceptance opportunity with Northwestern University at Northwestern University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Fellow PC - Psychiatry & Psychology - Singh lab — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Mayo Clinic Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Fellow PC - Psychiatry & Psychology - Singh lab opportunity with Mayo Clinic at Mayo Clinic.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate I, Analytical Development — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear ImmunityBio, Inc. Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate I, Analytical Development opportunity with ImmunityBio, Inc. at ImmunityBio, Inc..

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Park, #602 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Park, #602 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University of Texas, #1630 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Park, #602 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Park, #602 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Laboratory Research Technician — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear CHEManager International Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Laboratory Research Technician opportunity with CHEManager International at CHEManager International.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in CLIENT SERVICE COORDINATOR — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the CLIENT SERVICE COORDINATOR opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Survey Research Associate — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear A Full Renovation – Interiors & Design Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Survey Research Associate opportunity with A Full Renovation – Interiors & Design at A Full Renovation – Interiors & Design.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in B1 Team Member Trainer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Target Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the B1 Team Member Trainer opportunity with Target at Target.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Human Resources Assistant (HRA) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Select Specialty Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Human Resources Assistant (HRA) opportunity with Select Specialty Hospital at Select Specialty Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Unit Secretary - Med Surg — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear San Gorgonio Memorial Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Unit Secretary - Med Surg opportunity with San Gorgonio Memorial Hospital at San Gorgonio Memorial Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Administrative Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Research Foundation of The City University of New York Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Assistant opportunity with Research Foundation of The City University of New York at Research Foundation of The City University of New York.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear IXL Learning Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate University Recruiter opportunity with IXL Learning at IXL Learning.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Associate Scientist - Lab Automation
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. The Associate Scientist will contribute to the development, operation, and continuous improvement of automated capabilities that enable the scalable and reproducible generation of disease-relevant models. Working closely with scientists across discovery biology, translational biology, and other functional areas within BMS, this individual will help advance next-generation human disease modeling capabilities. This will be done through the application of advanced automation and human cell-based systems to accelerate neuroscience drug discovery. Key responsibilities: Support neuroscience drug discovery through the development, scale-up, and delivery of human iPSC-derived and other disease-relevant cellular model systems. Establish and maintain robust processes for cell line management, model characterization, quality control, and reproducibility. Collaborate with scientists across discovery teams to provide assay-ready cellular models and support the application of human disease models to target validation and therapeutic discovery programs. Manage the day-to-day operation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of automated laboratory platforms that enable scalable human disease modeling and support discovery research workflows. Contribute to the evaluation, development, and adoption of next-generation model systems and experimental approaches that expand understanding of disease mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities. Maintain high standards of scientific rigor, operational excellence, and data quality while supporting the continuous advancement of human disease modeling capabilities across the neuroscience portfolio. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, or a related scientific discipline. Experience: 0-2 years of laboratory experience in academia or industry.>1 year hands-on experience with: Mammalian cell culture and cellular model systems. Laboratory automation platforms, liquid handlers, high-content imaging systems, or related technologies. Cellular and molecular biology techniques used for model development and characterization Preferred technical and scientific skills Experience operating liquid handlers (Hamilton and/or Beckman Coulter), integrated workcells (HighRes), high-content imaging systems, or related laboratory automation technologies. Experience with human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) culture, differentiation, and characterization. Familiarity with biological characterization techniques such as immunofluorescence, qPCR, ELISA, or related assays. Hamilton or Biomek programming experience. Experience with laboratory orchestration software such as Cellario or Momentum. Familiarity with electronic laboratory notebook platforms such as Benchling. Experience with Python or other programming languages. Familiarity with data analysis, workflow automation, or scripting approaches that support laboratory operations Work Environment: On-site, in-lab. The job requires spending some amount of the day on your feet. We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. Compensation Overview: Cambridge Crossing: $97,120 - $117,688 The starting pay range(s) listed above is for full-time employees (FTE). You may also be eligible for additional discretionary incentive cash and stock opportunities. We determine starting pay thoughtfully – carefully considering the nature of the role, required skills, work location, schedule and the knowledge and experience you bring. Final compensation is guided by pay equity principles and applicable employment laws. Compensation programs are reviewed on an ongoing basis and may be adjusted over time to reflect evolving market factors, and individual, team or Company performance. Benefits: Subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans then in effect, you may be eligible to participate in our comprehensive benefit plans – including wellbeing support, retirement and financial protection benefits, and insurance offerings (medical, dental, vision, life and disability). U.S.-based exempt employees are eligible for Flexible Time Off (FTO), which provides paid time off without a set accrual limit, subject to manager approval, along with 11 paid company holidays each year. Non-exempt employees, RayzeBio employees, and employees located in Puerto Rico receive 160 hours of paid vacation annually for new hires (subject to manager approval), 11 paid company holidays, and 3 optional holidays. Depending on eligibility, employees may also have access to additional time-off benefits, including paid sick leave, up to two paid volunteer days per year, summer hours flexibility, and leaves of absence for medical, personal, parental, caregiver, bereavement, or military needs. Eligible employees also enjoy an annual Global Shutdown between Christmas Day and New Year's Day. Dear School District of Onalaska Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Assistant - OHS Attendance opportunity with School District of Onalaska at School District of Onalaska.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

$91,500.00 per year Overview A COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGIST position is available in the laboratory of Dr. Yana Pikman (https://pikmanlab.dana-farber.org/) at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Our research focuses on the application of clinical genomics for development of targeted therapy approaches for acute leukemia, drug testing and combination screening with the ultimate goals of 1) improving understanding of leukemia biology and 2) translating bench discovery to clinical care. We are also interested in studies of resistance to existing and emerging cancer therapies, and using data from leukemia models to inform mechanisms of resistance that can be further tested in the lab. You will join a team of investigators leading these efforts in the academic environment, work on the analysis of new and existing genomic datasets to advance efforts in identifying pediatric leukemia dependencies and informing leukemia drug sensitivity and resistance. You will collaborate closely with scientists as well as clinical researchers. You will play an essential, and possibly leading, role in project-focused work. The qualified candidate will carry out data analysis, develop and support data processing and analysis tools, create new algorithms for emerging clinically focused needs with an emphasis on bulk and single cell tumor analysis including Whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing analysis of leukemia samples, maintain datasets and databases, and facilitate the display and the distribution of processed data. We are looking for candidates with a minimum of two years of availability. Located in Boston and the surrounding communities, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is a leader in life changing breakthroughs in cancer research and patient care. We are united in our mission of conquering cancer, HIV/AIDS, and related diseases. We strive to create an inclusive, diverse, and equitable environment where we provide compassionate and comprehensive care to patients of all backgrounds, and design programs to promote public health particularly among high-risk and underserved populations. We conduct groundbreaking research that advances treatment, we educate tomorrow's physician/researchers, and we work with amazing partners, including other Harvard Medical School-affiliated hospitals. MINIMUM JOB QUALIFICATIONS: Minimum Education: Bachelor's degree required in a STEM field. Master’s degree preferred in bioinformatics, computational biology, statistics, biostatistics, computer science and/or the life sciences. Minimum Experience: 1 year with Bachelor’s degree or 0 years with Master’s degree; academic research experience or authorship in scientific publications experience may substitute for work experience. PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Data Processing: Uses existing tools to build data processing pipelines to convert raw data into formats compatible with conventional statistical analysis and visualization. Data Analysis: Performs routine analysis for which established tools exist and are considered reliable. Keep up with the computational biology literature to assure pipelines components are up to date. Data and Software Management: Monitors, downloads, organize, and manages data from public data repositories or generated by collaborates. Evaluates published tools and updates pipeline as necessary. Manuscript Preparation: Drafts the computational biology sections of a manuscript; assists in writing the results section; checks manuscripts for numerical accuracy; prepares tables and figures. Grant Preparation: Helps to formulate specific aims, explains options for experimental design, and develops data analysis plans. Research Portfolio Management: Develops timelines and components for multiple routine projects; masters multi-tasking so that complex projects involving many interdisciplinary individuals move forward smoothly. Team Interactions: Offers peer-to-peer training in design, analysis, and presentation of results. It is expected that insight into career growth will be offered to more junior computational biologists. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES REQUIRED: Computational Skills: Significant experience in computer programming and computational biological applications (experience in R and/ or Python, as well as cloud computing) Data Analysis Skills: Familiarity with principles of experimental design and the modern data analysis paradigms is required. A strong background in statistics and biology is required Collaboration: Able to discuss and present results, share ideas accurately and communicate them effectively, both in writing and verbally. Strong Interpersonal Skills: ability to effectively interact with all levels of staff and external contacts. Excellent analytical, organizational and time management skills. At Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, we work every day to create an innovative, caring, and inclusive environment where every patient, family, and staff member feels they belong. As relentless as we are in our mission to reduce the burden of cancer for all, we are committed to having faculty and staff who offer multifaceted experiences. Cancer knows no boundaries and when it comes to hiring the most dedicated and compassionate professionals, neither do we. If working in this kind of organization inspires you, we encourage you to apply. cold_email.subject: Interest in Computational Biologist - Dr. Yana Pikman Lab — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Computational Biologist - Dr. Yana Pikman Lab opportunity with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

I am especially interested in the lab's use of single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data to connect molecular mechanisms with therapeutic questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built reproducible genomics workflows and enjoy translating complex biological questions into clear, testable computational analyses.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator - Part Time — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator - Part Time opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Automation Scientist Intern, RAC Operations
jobs.description: Our mission is to make biology easier to engineer. Ginkgo is constructing, editing, and redesigning the living world in order to answer the globe’s growing challenges in health, energy, food, materials, and more. Our bioengineers make use of an in-house automated foundry for designing and building new organisms. The role is based out of Ginkgo’s Boston, MA location and requires regular in-person attendance. About the Role: Ginkgo Bioworks is deploying a massive fleet of Reconfigurable Automation Cells (RACs) —modular, mobile robotic units that snap together like LEGOs to form an autonomous lab. We are looking for an Automation Scientist Intern to be the hands-on force behind this fleet. You will learn how to load, operate, take down, and troubleshoot protocol runs on the most advanced lab automation hardware in the world, pushing our "Nebula" frontier lab towards autonomous operation. Responsibilities: Master the RAC Platform: Learn to operate and maintain a system of Reconfigurable Automation Cells, designed to support a variety of molecular and cell biology scientific workflows. You will queue and submit programmatically-generated protocols, remote monitor for errors and conduct remote and on-site error recovery, with the support of our Apex Support team. Over time, you will advance to modifying or writing new protocols for our RAC Automation system. jobs.title: Staff Scientist, Machine Learning (Genomics)
jobs.description: Natera is seeking a highly motivated Staff Machine Learning Scientist to join our rapidly growing company. As a member of the Data Science research team you will participate in the design and prototyping of cutting edge algorithms for analysis of genetic and clinical data. You will perform data analysis, algorithm design, contribute to our intellectual property portfolio, and interact closely with R&D and product teams to define the requirements and improve the products and processes. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: ML/DL Research Leadership: Lead research on machine learning and deep learning models using NGS data. Frame the problem, choose the approach, and decide when a model has earned the next round of investment. This is an individual contributor role with Staff-level scope. You will set the technical direction of the work, not just carry out a plan someone else wrote. Algorithm and Model Development: Design, build, and benchmark the models and features behind the next generation of Women Health and Organ Health products. Apply statistical learning and deep learning to high-dimensional, noisy, often small-sample sequencing data. Know when a simpler method is the right answer. Working with Bioinformatics Pipelines: Work directly with the existing sequencing pipelines and their outputs without needing a bioinformatician to run, change, or interpret them for you. When results look wrong, trace the problem back through each processing step and work out whether it comes from the pipeline, the data, or the biology. Build or extend pipeline components when a project needs it. Study Design and Experimental Partnership: Work with molecular biology and assay development scientists to design experiments. Help decide what data to generate, how much of it, and with what controls so the analysis can answer the question. Troubleshoot experiments alongside the lab, and tell a biology problem from a data or analysis problem. Rigor and Documentation: Set the standard for careful analysis on the team: sound validation design, honest performance estimates, no leakage between training and evaluation data, and documentation. Support the group in producing high-quality technical and design documentation. Intellectual Property and Scientific Contribution: Contribute to Natera's IP portfolio through invention disclosures and patent work, and to its scientific reputation through publications and presentations where appropriate. Technical Leadership and Mentorship: Mentor data scientists and bioinformaticians, review their work, and be the person others bring hard modeling questions to. Make decisions about your own methods with minimal direction, including when the problem is ambiguous, and know when to escalate. Ways of Working: AI is a routine part of the work here, including coding agents for implementation, analysis, and review. You own what you ship, whatever produced it. We do not screen for prior experience with these tools, and we provide the tooling and the ramp time. QUALIFICATIONS: M.S. or Ph.D. in a quantitative field such as Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Engineering, or similar. Equivalent depth built through work counts fully. 6+ years of hands-on experience in machine learning and data analysis on biological or genomic data after your degree. We count relevant experience from the point your work became substantially independent, however you got there. A demonstrated track record of models or algorithms you led that reached real use (a product, a production pipeline, or a decision someone relied on), not only a result. We are hiring for depth in NGS, bioinformatics, and machine learning, and we will provide the domain ramp. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Depth in next-generation sequencing data analysis: sequencing QC, alignment and quantification, normalization, and the artifacts that come with them. You should have the judgment to spot a wrong result before someone else does. Working fluency with NGS bioinformatics pipelines. You can run them on your own, read their code and logs, follow a result back through each processing step, and diagnose failures or unexpected outputs. You can also build or modify pipeline components when needed. Extensive practical experience with machine learning, deep learning, and statistics, including model validation and performance estimation on limited or imbalanced data. Advanced Python, including open-source ML libraries (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost) in a cloud environment. Experience processing large datasets and working with a query language such as SQL. A proven ability to apply mathematical and statistical principles to real estimation problems and turn them into practical solutions. Familiarity with assay development and analysis pipelines for molecular or clinical biomarkers. Clear communication of technical results to people who do not share your background, and a record of delivering complex projects with cross-functional teams. PREFFERED SKILLS: Experience with RNA-seq, small RNA/miRNA. Experience building probabilistic models for NGS and omics data. Experience with diagnostic product development in a regulated or CLIA/CAP setting. Experience with workflow orchestration (Nextflow, WDL, Snakemake) and containerization (Docker), enough to read, debug, and extend existing workflows. AWS or GCP for large-scale ML training and inference. Patents, peer-reviewed publications, or conference presentations. A desire to work in a fast-paced environment where a small team has high impact. The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. Remote USA $167,400 — $209,200 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! cold_email.subject: Interest in Staff Scientist, Machine Learning (Genomics) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Staff Scientist, Machine Learning (Genomics) opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the group's effort to integrate multi-omic and clinical data with AI for biomarker and therapeutic discovery. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in bioinformatics, pipeline development, and an LLM-assisted competency-mapping project has made me especially interested in rigorous, interpretable AI for biomedical data.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Histology Lab Operator I
jobs.description: POSITION SUMMARY: The Histology Lab Operator I is a member of the Histopathology Department responsible for assisting HT/HTLs in analyzing specimens and maintaining equipment in good condition. The position is for First shift 6.00 AM- 2.30 PM and third shift 10.00 PM- 6.30 AM. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: • Assists certified/licensed personnel in clinical patient testing in accordance with the SOP • Perform histological preparations for the tissue whole exome sequencing laboratory with little to no errors • Duties may include but not limited to: preparation of tissues, stained slides, macrodissection and supporting workflow tasks • Sets up equipment and assists with automated lab procedures, as applicable • Assist and complete daily tasks • Maintains equipment and instruments in good operating condition • Maintain sufficient inventory of material, supplies, and equipment in the laboratory for the performance of duties • Documents information accurately and in accordance with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) • Performs other duties as assigned QUALIFICATIONS: • 0-2 years of experience • An associate's, or higher, degree in a histotechnician program OR An associate's degree, or higher, in one of the chemical or biological sciences AND one year of experience and/or training in histology within the past 5 years OR - completion of a course of training of at least nine months in a histotechnician program OR A bachelor's, or higher, degree in one of the chemical or biological sciences, including a combination of thirty (30) hours in biology and chemistry; and either one of the following conditions: - one year of experience and/or training in histology within the past 5 years OR - completion of a course of training of at least nine months in a histotechnician program • A copy of the degree is required at the time of hire; the degree must either be from the US or equivalent to a US degree KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: • Excellent interpersonal, communication, computer, and technical skills • Excellent oral and written communication skills • Word processing and data management • Ability to work well in a group • Adhere to the department's time and attendance guidelines PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT: • Duties typically performed in BSL-2 laboratory with potentially hazardous material • Standing or sitting for long periods of time may be necessary • Duties may require working weekends and overtime • Must be able to lift boxes or supplies up to 35 lbs. • Duties require wearing safety goggles, gloves, and laboratory coat. • Duties require exposure to cold air due to frequent accessing of refrigeration and/or freezer units. • Repetitive hand motion may be necessary Compensation & Total Rewards This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and skills considerations. This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including: Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision) 401(k) with company match Generous paid time off and company holidays Additional wellness and work-life benefits Compensation Range $23.06 — $34.56 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. cold_email.subject: Interest in Histology Lab Operator I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Histology Lab Operator I opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Work with large-scale structured and unstructured datasets including clinical data, publications, real-world evidence, and other healthcare datasets. Build predictive models and advanced analytics solutions to generate actionable insights and support data-driven decision making. Develop LLM-powered applications such as AI assistants, knowledge-grounded reasoning systems, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. Develop and maintain semantic layers, ontologies, and contextual data frameworks that enable consistent interpretation of data across AI systems and analytics workflows. Implement evaluation frameworks for AI systems, response quality assessment, hallucination mitigation, and benchmark-driven validation. Partner with data engineering and platform teams to ensure scalable pipelines, high-quality data availability, and production-ready AI systems. Communicate analytical findings and AI-driven insights clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders through reports, visualizations, and presentations. Strong programming proficiency in Python for data science and AI system development Experience working with modern data platforms such as Databricks (Spark, MLflow, Delta Lake). Experience building LLM-based applications, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI copilots, and knowledge-grounded AI systems. Experience implementing embedding pipelines and vector database architectures (e.g., FAISS, Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch Vector, pgvector). Experience developing and deploying AI or ML services using FastAPI or similar frameworks for scalable APIs. Proficiency in working with large datasets using SQL and distributed data processing frameworks. Excellent communication and presentation skills to convey complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience Btech/Masters in a relevant fields such as Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science or a related discipline. 3+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, or applied AI roles. jobs.title: Field AI Engineer
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Position Summary We are seeking a curious, hands-on engineer to join our Global Sales Systems and Capabilities team within CBI&T (Commercial Business Insights & Technology) in Hyderabad. This role is focused on building AI-powered capabilities for our field force on Veeva Vault CRM – from LLM-based assistants and agentic workflows to the data pipelines and integrations that ground them in trusted commercial data. The ideal candidate has 2–4 years of experience in software or data engineering with Python, SQL and AWS, and at least 1 year of hands-on experience taking LLM/GenAI features from prototype to production. This is an applied AI engineering role – deep ML research or model-training experience is not required; what matters most is a builder with a product mindset who cares whether what they ship is used and trusted by field users. If you want an exciting and rewarding career that is meaningful, consider joining our diverse team! Key Responsibilities Design, build and ship AI/LLM-powered features for Vault CRM field users – such as pre-call insights, call note summarization, conversational assistants and next-best-action recommendations – using prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool/function calling and agentic workflows. Build and maintain the data foundation for AI: cloud-based (AWS) batch and event-driven pipelines (Glue, Lambda, API Gateway, EventBridge) and integrations with Vault CRM (e.g., Vault REST APIs, Direct Data API) and related commercial systems that supply clean, timely and governed context to AI applications. Implement retrieval components – document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector/hybrid search and metadata filtering – and tune them for relevance and accuracy. Integrate foundation models through enterprise platforms (e.g., Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) and expose AI capabilities through secure APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and/or native Vault CRM extensions. Make evaluation part of the build: create test datasets, define quality metrics (accuracy, groundedness, hallucination rate) and run automated and human-in-the-loop evaluations before and after each release. Monitor AI applications in production – tracing, latency, token cost and user feedback – and continuously improve prompts, retrieval and model choices based on what the data shows. Apply responsible AI guardrails appropriate for a regulated life sciences environment, including PII handling, content safety, access controls and commercial compliance considerations, in partnership with security, privacy and AI governance teams. Bring a product mindset: partner with field users, business stakeholders and product managers to understand workflows, shape use cases, build quick prototypes to validate value, and define success measures such as adoption, time saved and user satisfaction. Stay current with fast-evolving AI tools and practices, use AI-assisted development tools effectively, and share learnings with the broader Field Integrations team to raise AI fluency across the group. Participate in effort estimation, code reviews, CI/CD and production support, and maintain standard technical documentation such as design documents, deployment checklists and testing/validation records. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field. 2–4 years of IT experience in software development or data engineering, including at least 1 year of hands-on experience building LLM/GenAI applications (production experience preferred; strong project or POC work will be considered). Strong programming skills in Python, with sound engineering practices – clean code, testing, version control (Git) and CI/CD. Good SQL skills and understanding of relational databases (preferably PostgreSQL); experience building and consuming RESTful APIs. Hands-on experience with AWS services such as Lambda, API Gateway, Glue, S3 and EventBridge. Practical experience with LLM APIs and at least one orchestration/agent framework (e.g., LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Strands Agents, Bedrock Agents), including prompt engineering, structured outputs and tool/function calling. Understanding of RAG architecture, embeddings and vector stores (e.g., OpenSearch, pgvector). Familiarity with LLM evaluation and observability approaches and awareness of common failure modes such as hallucination, prompt injection and data leakage. Product mindset – ability to turn an ambiguous business problem into a well-scoped AI solution, explain trade-offs (quality, latency, cost) clearly to non-technical stakeholders, and iterate based on user feedback. Ability and willingness to learn new technologies quickly; proactive and self-motivated, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. Good to Have Experience with Veeva Vault CRM or Veeva CRM (Salesforce-based), Vault APIs, or other CRM platforms. VENDOR AND PARTNER GOVERNANCE · Manage PSP vendors, in-country delivery partners and other assigned service providers. · Set clear scopes, service measures, governance routines and escalation processes. · Coordinate contracting, purchase-order, invoice and performance-management requirements with relevant functions. 3. SAFETY, COMPLIANCE AND AUDIT READINESS · Partner with Safety to ensure appropriate adverse-event and product-quality reporting. · Coordinate Legal, Compliance, Medical and other required clearances. · Maintain complete, current and audit-ready program and operational documentation. · Escalate material patient, safety, quality, compliance or continuity risks promptly. 4. MARKETING OPERATIONS · Manage assigned CE&I purchase orders, vendors and invoicing. · Coordinate samples and launch operations through approved in-country vendors. · Support assigned events/congress, campaign or above-country marketing-operational requirements. · Establish practical workflows, service standards and controls for assigned operations. 5. CROSS-MARKET DELIVERY AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT · Maintain effective coordination between Egypt-based delivery and Saudi business owners and partners. · Plan required Saudi site visits and in-country governance touchpoints. · Identify opportunities to simplify operations, improve vendor performance and strengthen the patient experience. DECISION RIGHTS AND ROLE BOUNDARIES · Owns PSP operational governance and assigned marketing-operations delivery within approved strategy, budget and compliance requirements. · Marketing Execution Lead sets portfolio priorities and overall marketing-execution standards. · Medical/Safety/Legal/Compliance retain their respective professional accountabilities and approvals. · Does not own brand strategy, content creation or channel execution. CAPABILITIES AND QUALIFICATIONS · Bachelor's degree in pharmacy, Life Sciences, Healthcare Administration, Business or a related field. · Relevant experience in patient-support programs, pharmaceutical operations, marketing operations or vendor management. · Knowledge of regulated patient-program governance, safety reporting, and audit readiness. · Strong vendor, budget, purchase-order and operational project-management capability. · Ability to coordinate delivery across countries, partners and functions. · Strong risk judgment, communication and stakeholder-management skills. · Saudi-market experience is highly preferred. jobs.title: Staff Scientist, Machine Learning (Genomics)
jobs.description: Natera is seeking a highly motivated Staff Machine Learning Scientist to join our rapidly growing company. As a member of the Data Science research team you will participate in the design and prototyping of cutting edge algorithms for analysis of genetic and clinical data. You will perform data analysis, algorithm design, contribute to our intellectual property portfolio, and interact closely with R&D and product teams to define the requirements and improve the products and processes. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: ML/DL Research Leadership: Lead research on machine learning and deep learning models using NGS data. Frame the problem, choose the approach, and decide when a model has earned the next round of investment. This is an individual contributor role with Staff-level scope. You will set the technical direction of the work, not just carry out a plan someone else wrote. Algorithm and Model Development: Design, build, and benchmark the models and features behind the next generation of Women Health and Organ Health products. Apply statistical learning and deep learning to high-dimensional, noisy, often small-sample sequencing data. Know when a simpler method is the right answer. Working with Bioinformatics Pipelines: Work directly with the existing sequencing pipelines and their outputs without needing a bioinformatician to run, change, or interpret them for you. When results look wrong, trace the problem back through each processing step and work out whether it comes from the pipeline, the data, or the biology. Build or extend pipeline components when a project needs it. Study Design and Experimental Partnership: Work with molecular biology and assay development scientists to design experiments. Help decide what data to generate, how much of it, and with what controls so the analysis can answer the question. Troubleshoot experiments alongside the lab, and tell a biology problem from a data or analysis problem. Rigor and Documentation: Set the standard for careful analysis on the team: sound validation design, honest performance estimates, no leakage between training and evaluation data, and documentation. Support the group in producing high-quality technical and design documentation. Intellectual Property and Scientific Contribution: Contribute to Natera's IP portfolio through invention disclosures and patent work, and to its scientific reputation through publications and presentations where appropriate. Technical Leadership and Mentorship: Mentor data scientists and bioinformaticians, review their work, and be the person others bring hard modeling questions to. Make decisions about your own methods with minimal direction, including when the problem is ambiguous, and know when to escalate. Ways of Working: AI is a routine part of the work here, including coding agents for implementation, analysis, and review. You own what you ship, whatever produced it. We do not screen for prior experience with these tools, and we provide the tooling and the ramp time. QUALIFICATIONS: M.S. or Ph.D. in a quantitative field such as Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Engineering, or similar. Equivalent depth built through work counts fully. 6+ years of hands-on experience in machine learning and data analysis on biological or genomic data after your degree. We count relevant experience from the point your work became substantially independent, however you got there. A demonstrated track record of models or algorithms you led that reached real use (a product, a production pipeline, or a decision someone relied on), not only a result. We are hiring for depth in NGS, bioinformatics, and machine learning, and we will provide the domain ramp. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Depth in next-generation sequencing data analysis: sequencing QC, alignment and quantification, normalization, and the artifacts that come with them. You should have the judgment to spot a wrong result before someone else does. Working fluency with NGS bioinformatics pipelines. You can run them on your own, read their code and logs, follow a result back through each processing step, and diagnose failures or unexpected outputs. You can also build or modify pipeline components when needed. Extensive practical experience with machine learning, deep learning, and statistics, including model validation and performance estimation on limited or imbalanced data. Advanced Python, including open-source ML libraries (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost) in a cloud environment. Experience processing large datasets and working with a query language such as SQL. A proven ability to apply mathematical and statistical principles to real estimation problems and turn them into practical solutions. Familiarity with assay development and analysis pipelines for molecular or clinical biomarkers. Clear communication of technical results to people who do not share your background, and a record of delivering complex projects with cross-functional teams. PREFFERED SKILLS: Experience with RNA-seq, small RNA/miRNA. Experience building probabilistic models for NGS and omics data. Experience with diagnostic product development in a regulated or CLIA/CAP setting. Experience with workflow orchestration (Nextflow, WDL, Snakemake) and containerization (Docker), enough to read, debug, and extend existing workflows. AWS or GCP for large-scale ML training and inference. Patents, peer-reviewed publications, or conference presentations. A desire to work in a fast-paced environment where a small team has high impact. Compensation & Total Rewards This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations. This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including: Annual performance incentive bonus Long-term equity awards Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision) 401(k) with company match Generous paid time off and company holidays Additional wellness and work-life benefits Compensation Range $170,600 — $213,300 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Process Development Associate Scientist, Drug Product Visual Inspection Sciences opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. Best,
Celina Lin
